A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReFAT study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and matchable. V2 retains Appendices A–D and adds Appendices E–F.

before.justification: V1 reports original mechanistic analyses, adversarial robustness and utility evaluations, and model-response case studies in Sections 3–7 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds a LAT checkpoint evaluation in Table 1 and MMLU over-refusal measurements in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Refusal-feature estimation, periodic refresh, probabilistic ablation, and the safety/utility objectives are retained. V2 newly explains the training-time omission of the harmless-mean offset, but the earlier training equations already lacked that term. Algorithm 1 documents the existing procedure.

E1.justification: The training sources, HarmBench/AdvBench attack tasks, and MMLU, MT-Bench, and XSTest coverage remain unchanged. The added MMLU refusal assessment measures another outcome on an existing task; it introduces no distinct dataset, domain, or input scenario.

E2.justification: V2 adds Latent Adversarial Training (LAT) to the Llama-3-8B comparison in Table 1, using the checkpoint released by Sheshadri et al. The existing RT, R2D2, and CAT comparisons remain; LAT is not evaluated for Mistral or Gemma.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds a refusal-count evaluation on 5,700 MMLU questions. The new LAT comparison uses an externally fine-tuned checkpoint rather than the paper's controlled baseline-training procedure. Retained experiments keep their stated evaluation splits, attacks, and judges; the expanded tuning description does not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 supplements the existing XSTest over-refusal check with the MMLU analysis in Appendix F. It also adds qualitative sensitivity findings about ablation probability, layer selection, and baseline hyperparameters, while removing one response example from Table 2. The mechanistic, clamping, and multilingual-failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 2 retains the same 99% confidence intervals. V2 introduces no new seed or repeated-training-run information, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests; its added comparison and refusal-count results are point estimates.

E6.justification: All pre-existing numerical entries in Tables 1 and 5 and the results displayed in the figures are retained. V2 adds LAT scores, including 9.06% GCG ASR and 45.0% RFA ASR, and Table 6's MMLU refusal counts. Table 2 loses the government-database example without changing the remaining qualitative findings.

T1.justification: The refusal-feature definitions, intervention equations, safety score, minimax objective, and perturbation-optimality definition are retained. Equation 10 equivalently expands the Bernoulli expectation into probability-weighted terms. The expanded single-direction explanation restates the existing setup; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims: a shared refusal-ablation mechanism, approximate worst-case perturbations, and efficient robustness improvements while preserving utility. The added evaluations support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly acknowledges that limited hyperparameter searches may leave better utility–robustness trade-offs undiscovered. Section 4.2 explains the efficiency rationale for omitting the training-time mean offset. The ethics statement adds concerns about overconfidence and operator-driven content suppression; the existing multilingual limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds pseudocode, explicit training-versus-inference behavior, and tuning details covering 40 AdvBench examples and four probability and layer-selection choices. It removes the main text's conflicting universal LoRA rank of 64 while retaining Table 4's ranks of 128/128/64. Table 4's beta_u values are deleted; pRFA = 0.5 remains documented in prose.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to DrAttack, WordGame, Cao et al.'s robust alignment checking, and Cao et al.'s personalized steering. It also explicitly distinguishes ReFAT's training-time intervention from inference-time steering. The central positioning connecting adversarial training and representation engineering remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify refusal-feature projection, training and evaluation, and XSTest reference answers. V2 adds ethics and reproducibility statements, expands Appendix A, and introduces Appendices E–F while regrouping existing appendix explanations. Most of the original narrative and section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Algorithm 1 and Table 6, inserts the LAT row into Table 1, removes a Table 2 example, resizes Tables 2–3, and removes two rows from Table 4. Figure 5, Table 5, and appendix material are repositioned, and conference headers are added. All 19 figure graphics are retained.

improvement.justification: The relevant LAT comparison and complementary MMLU over-refusal check modestly strengthen the empirical assessment. Pseudocode, implementation explanations, and explicit tuning limitations improve transparency. These gains outweigh limited documentation regressions, including deleted beta_u values and incorrect cross-references and Gemma labels. The externally trained LAT checkpoint and unchanged central results limit the extent of the improvement.
